author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed. Ported the canonical jmap-mail-server HashMap<Id, IdFate>-based dedup pattern (crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/mod.rs:657-680) to calendars-server. Vec::contains O(n²) → HashMap O(1) lookups, eliminating the textbook 'Vec used as set' anti-pattern the bead flags. Added IdFate enum at memory.rs:124-143 mirroring the canonical. Preserved JMAP-ic0j.15's recycling debug_assert at semantically-equivalent positions (fates.get(id) returns Some(IdFate::Destroyed) is the new equivalent of destroyed.contains(id) in Vec form).

Semantic-behavior preservation: the canonical mail-server takes RFC 8620 §5.2's SHOULD-preferred path (omit create+destroy-in-window ids from both buckets); calendars-server's previous Vec-based code took the §5.2 MAY path (include in 'destroyed' only). Filed bd:JMAP-ic0j.75 as a follow-up to track the SHOULD-vs-MAY semantic alignment — switching paths is a separate scope-bounded decision and was not pursued here because the bead is labeled 'idiomatic-rust' / 'iterators', not 'api-contract'. The preserved MAY-path behavior keeps the existing dedup_pass_does_not_panic_on_distinct_recreated_ids test (memory.rs:1419) passing.

Added a final sort_by step on each result bucket so output is deterministic across HashMap iteration order (HashMap iteration order is non-deterministic per std docs; the canonical mail-server tests appear to tolerate the non-determinism via single-element-bucket assertions, but explicit sort is safer and costs nothing).

Verified: cargo fmt clean, clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test --all-features 120+13+1 passed (including all three change_log_dedup_tests).
